Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

elsar 0.4.2

Values change: rebuild these layers

0.4.2 fixes several calculations that gave wrong values without any error. Layers built with 0.4.1 or earlier should be rebuilt; the pipeline should stay on 0.4.1 until a country is rerun.

  • Every layer that goes through make_normalised_raster() (almost all feature layers). Inputs are now aggregated to the planning units with the requested method (method_override: "mean", "sum", "max", "mode", …), weighting every input cell by the share of the planning unit it covers. Before, they were warped onto the planning grid with bilinear interpolation first, which made method_override a no-op, point-sampled proportion layers (agriculture, built areas, LULC classes) and blurred coarse inputs. Inputs in another CRS are aggregated through a sub-grid of up to 10 x 10 cells per planning unit (area-weighted to within 1/100 of a planning unit, with bounded memory, also across the antimeridian).

  • Layers with gaps inside the planning units. Missing data is now filled (fill_na) after inversion and rescaling, so it always gets the lowest score. Before, it was filled first: inverted layers ranked missing data highest, and the fill value stretched the rescale of other layers. For a layer with negative values (e.g. a difference), missing cells now score the same as the lowest value instead of mid-scale.

  • Constant layers (e.g. a region fully covered by protected areas, or an all-1 zone) are no longer turned into NaN by rescale_raster(); they become 1 (or 0 when the value is 0), with a message.

  • Zones built from LULC, degradation or pasture rasters (make_protect_zone(), make_restore_zone(), make_manage_zone(), make_urban_greening_zone(), make_urban_greening_opportunities()). Thresholds such as agriculture_threshold = 0.1 are now compared with the true share of each planning unit. Before, these paths rescaled the share to the national maximum first, so the threshold meant something different in every country. Pasture probability given as a percentage (0-100, as in the Global Pasture Watch layers) is divided by 100 first, so pasturelands_threshold = 0.35 means a 35% probability (new pasturelands_scale, "auto" by default).

  • Layers whose values are all zero or negative (e.g. differences) are no longer mistaken for empty layers and returned as all 0.

  • make_urban_greening_opportunities() inverted NDVI twice, ranking green cells as most in need of greening; low vegetation now ranks highest and water lowest. It also no longer requires the planning-unit layer to be named “Planning Units”.

  • KBA layers (make_kbas()). Point KBAs are now buffered to their reported area: repareakm2 is in km², but was converted as hectares, so the circles were 100 times too small.

  • Wetlands and Ramsar (make_wetlands_ramsar()). Ramsar polygons are now always rasterised, with buffered points added when buffer_points = TRUE (centroids of sites that also have a boundary are ignored, via the new id_column, so those sites are not counted twice). Before, they were only rasterised when the data contained points and buffer_points = FALSE, so Ramsar sites were usually missing. Any positive wetland class now counts as wetland, so 0/1 wetland masks work (the CIFOR map, coded 10-100, is unaffected).

  • Protected areas with buffer_points = FALSE (make_protected_areas()). When the data contained points, only the first protected-area polygon was rasterised; all are now included.

  • Protected areas and indigenous lands with point data (convert_points_polygon()). Polygons whose reported area is 0 or missing (common in WDPCA) are no longer dropped, and a multipoint’s reported area is shared between its points instead of given to each (also when points and multipoints are mixed).

  • Threatened and under-represented ecosystems, urban heat (exact_rasterise()). fun = mean averaged each planning unit over all features, including ones not touching it, and the method changed above 1,000 features. It is now the coverage-weighted mean of the features present, with one rule for any number of features. max and min no longer shrink at the edges of features. (With tens of thousands of features it is slower than the old approximate path; the callers in elsar pass tens to hundreds.)

  • Restore Zone (make_restore_zone()). It is now the intended band of degraded but restorable land: (degradation > degradation_threshold | HII >= hii_min) & HII < hii_max, excluding farmland and built-up areas (they are managed, not restored). The upper cap (hii_max, default 21 on the HII’s 0-50 scale, as in the original ELSA design) had been lost, so land under very high pressure was included. human_pressure_threshold is deprecated in favour of hii_min. The degradation input can now be a 0/1 degraded-areas layer as well as an SDG 15.3.1 layer (-1 = degraded): before, a 0/1 layer such as make_degraded_areas() output silently added no degradation. degradation_encoding = "auto" reads the values within the planning region and stops when they are unclear. This affects any 0/1 “Degraded Areas” input, not only compute_degraded_areas. Note: the new arguments come before agriculture_threshold, so positional calls shift.

  • All zones with filter_patch_size = TRUE. Removing small patches used terra::sieve(), which also filled small excluded holes (farms, towns) back into the zone, and could keep small patches next to other small patches or NoData. Small eligible patches are now removed exactly and excluded cells always stay excluded. Patches are now edge-connected: cells touching only at a corner count as separate patches (they were joined before).

  • Planning-unit grids (make_planning_units()). The grid now covers the whole boundary: its extent is snapped outwards to whole cells, where before up to one cell along the east and north edges could be lost. Grids can gain a row or column, so every layer should be rebuilt on the new grid.

  • Countries crossing the antimeridian (Fiji, Kiribati, Russia, New Zealand with the Chathams, the US with the Aleutians, the US Minor Outlying Islands). The custom Mollweide projection was centred near 0 degrees instead of on the country, which stretched it across the whole projection (Fiji and Russia could not get planning units at all). Other regions keep their centre, including wide ones that straddle 0 degrees (e.g. France with overseas territories). Kiribati’s planning units are slow to build at the default threshold (minutes, several GB): consider a lower pu_threshold.

  • limit_to_mainland = TRUE. In make_boundary() it kept the largest province when the boundary had several features; it now merges them and keeps the largest polygon. In make_planning_units() it was accepted but ignored; it now drops islands. “Mainland” is the single largest polygon: the South Island for New Zealand, the contiguous states for the US.

  • Calibrated weights with lock-ins (elsar_calibrate_weights()). PA lock-ins are now enforced, as in the original ELSA pre-calibration: locked cells are added to their zone and removed from every other zone, including do_nothing. Before, lock-ins only raised the zone’s budget, so the weights were fitted to a problem without the lock-in that the ELSA tool solves (in a test, none of the locked cells went to Protect). Calibrations made since the December 2025 rewrite should be rerun. Zone masks given as 0/1 (as the zone builders return) are now read as 1/NA; a 0 used to make an ineligible cell available. New lockin_threshold (default 0.1, as in the ELSA tool) and lockin_priority (overlapping lock-ins go to the zone with the lowest raster value, as in the tool: protect, manage, restore, urban greening). A zone’s budget floor now counts the locked cells, so fractional lock-ins no longer make the problem infeasible.

  • Forest integrity (make_forest_integrity()). FLII (published on a 0-10000 scale) and FSII are now each rescaled to 0-1 before they are averaged; before, FLII swamped FSII. Inputs that are all 0 give an all-0 layer with a warning instead of NaN.

  • Flood abatement opportunities (make_flood_abatement_opportunities()). Now rescale(flood_risk * (1 - NDVI)): flood-prone land lacking vegetation scores highest (where restoring, managing or greening it can reduce floods; the ELSA impacts credit the layer fully to those actions and half to protect), water 0. The old flood_risk / (1 - NDVI) inverted this (it rose with vegetation) and grew without bound for dense vegetation. NDVI is used on its own 0-1 scale, not rescaled within the region.

  • Underrepresented ecosystems (make_underrepresented_ecosystems()). The value is now each planning unit’s largest gap to the 30% target divided by the target (0 = target met, 1 = unprotected), as published (“30% minus the protected percent”). Before, the gaps were rescaled across ecosystems, so the largest gap in the region became 1 however small it was, and a region with a single ecosystem (such as Andorra) became a constant 1.

  • Threatened ecosystems for protection (make_threatened_ecosystems_protection()). Ecosystems in another CRS than the planning units gave an all-NA layer (the intact-area mask was relabelled instead of transformed).

  • Layers written with save_raster(). Each data type now has its own NoData value and predictor: FLT8S failed, and in INT2U/INT4U data the valid value 255 was written as NoData.

  • get_binary_layers() tests each layer exactly: near-0 or near-1 floats were classed as binary (and then written as integers, losing them), and an all-NA layer shifted the labels of the others.

Other changes

  • elsar is now released under the Apache License 2.0 (was CC BY 4.0, which is not meant for software), as agreed by the authors.

  • make_postgres_connection() is back (it was removed in 0.4.0 without deprecation, but existing code, including the pipeline, calls it). It returns a named list.

  • get_coverage() counts the zone only inside the planning units, whether cells outside are NA or 0 (it could exceed 100%).

  • crop_global_raster() returns an empty layer only when the input does not overlap the planning units; other errors are raised instead of becoming an all-0 layer.

  • filter_sf() and elsar_load_data() warn when an ISO3 filter matches no features (usually a wrong iso3_column); multi-layer loads warn once, only if nothing matched. sf’s “layer is ignored” warning is gone.

  • save_raster() returns the file path invisibly and no longer emits GDAL’s “MEM driver does not support creation option” warnings.

  • make_planning_units() accepts boundaries with several features (it failed when estimating the cell size), and grows the cell size when the first estimate gives too many planning units instead of stopping with an error.

  • ISO3 codes are matched regardless of case, both the argument (e.g. "npl") and the codes in the data; before, a case mismatch silently matched nothing.

  • make_manage_zone() works without a pasture layer (pasturelands = NULL, the documented default, used to fail), and its alternative zone (v2, agriculture and pasture) now also excludes built-up areas, like the default zone.

  • make_protect_zone() accepts protected areas as a multi-row SpatVector and in any CRS; the docs no longer claim that NULL loads protected areas.

  • exact_rasterise() accepts fun as mean, sum, max or min (function, terra generic or string); other functions now give an error. cores and max_exact_features are ignored. With no features it returns zeros. It accepts SpatVector input, uses a factor attribute’s labels (not its level codes), rejects non-numeric attributes and ignores non-polygon geometry.

  • make_kbas() and make_wetlands_ramsar() require an iso3 column and say so, instead of silently keeping every site worldwide when it is missing. make_kbas() no longer fails when excluding AZE sites leaves no sites (it returns, and saves, an empty layer), and geometries are re-validated after reprojection.

  • make_managed_forests() gains rescaled (default TRUE). When its output feeds make_manage_zone(), use rescaled = FALSE: the zone’s forest_class_threshold is a true share of each planning unit.

  • make_normalised_raster(): cells outside the planning units are now always NoData, also with fill_na = NULL (which leaves gaps inside them NA).

  • make_normalised_raster() names its output layer after name_out (or the input layer), and also saves the empty layer it returns when there is no data.

  • R CMD check now runs on the develop branch and on pull requests into it.

elsar 0.4.1

Bug fixes

  • make_underrepresented_ecosystems() gave ecosystems that no protected area overlaps an NA gap, which ended up as the lowest value after rasterising. They now get the full gap (they are 0% protected), so the least-protected ecosystems score highest, as intended. Layers built with earlier versions under-rate completely unprotected ecosystems and should be rebuilt.

  • Countries with no usable protected-area geometry (no records, none inside the planning units, or only points without a reported area, e.g. Somalia in WDPA) no longer fail:

    • make_protected_areas() returns an all-0 layer and a 0-row sf, with a warning that says why. New argument return_sf returns the cleaned polygons for a supplied sf_in too (default unchanged).
    • make_protect_zone() accepts 0-row protected areas; it then needs a fixed hii_threshold, since there is nothing to derive it from.
    • make_underrepresented_ecosystems() accepts 0-row protected areas and warns that the result is uniform (1 wherever there is an ecosystem).

  • make_protected_areas() now re-validates geometries after reprojecting to the planning-unit CRS and before dissolving. Reprojection can turn polygons that were valid in the source CRS invalid, and dissolving them failed with a GEOS TopologyException: side location conflict (seen with California’s 30x30 Conserved Areas layer; 77 polygons broke on reprojection).

  • elsar now loads the sf namespace when it is loaded, so sf’s S3 methods (e.g. [.sf, filter.sf) are registered. Previously the package referred to sf only via sf:: and never imported from it, so sf’s namespace was not loaded at package-load time. As a result, operations on sf objects - including subsetting the bundled boundary_dat and the dplyr calls inside make_boundary() - could dispatch to the wrong method and fail with a vctrs “incompatible scalar type” error unless sf happened to be loaded some other way (e.g. library(sf)). Surfaced by running the tests against the installed package under R CMD check.

  • make_planning_units() now errors clearly when boundary_proj is in a geographic (lat/long) CRS or has no CRS. Previously a lat/long boundary was silently rasterised into a single cell (the metre resolution was interpreted as degrees) and every downstream step ran on that one cell with no error or warning. Use make_boundary(custom_projection = TRUE) (the default) to get a suitable projected boundary.

  • make_boundary(limit_to_mainland = TRUE) now works. It previously always errored (sf::st_area() was called on an rlang data pronoun). It now keeps the single largest polygon, and does so after any iso3 filter, so the mainland is chosen within the target region rather than across the whole input dataset. The result is also normalised to WGS84 as the non-mainland path already was.

  • make_boundary() now errors with an actionable message (listing the available codes) when iso3 matches no feature, instead of silently returning a 0-row sf (or later failing with a cryptic GDAL projection error). It also checks that iso3_column / col_name are actually columns in the input, and that the boundary has a coordinate reference system before reprojecting it.

  • elsar_load_data() no longer silently returns a non-sf object when reads fail. When loading multiple files/layers it now errors if every read fails (previously it returned a 0 x 0 tibble while logging “Loaded 0 features”), and warns but continues when only some fail, naming them. Loading a single unreadable file now errors instead of returning NULL. Relatedly, filter_sf() now honours its “return NULL on failure” contract for corrupt files: the layer-name probe (sf::st_layers()) is now inside the read guard, so a bad file is skipped rather than aborting the whole load. When the successfully-read layers have different coordinate reference systems, the load now stops with a clear message naming them instead of failing deep inside bind_rows().

  • elsar_load_data()’s PostgreSQL path now works. The connection list is spliced into DBI::dbConnect() via do.call() instead of the rlang !!! operator, which never worked there (dbConnect() is a plain S4 generic, so !!!x was parsed as !(!(!x))). The path now also guards on RPostgres/DBI with an install hint, closes the connection with on.exit(), quotes table/column identifiers and the iso3 literal to prevent SQL injection, and omits the WHERE clause when no iso3/iso3_column is supplied.

New features

  • elsar_calibrate_weights() computes per-feature calibration weights for an ELSA prioritization so that features achieve more even representation relative to their single-feature maxima. This is the ELSA pre-calibration step, previously living in the downstream tool; the objective and framework are unchanged (spread-of-shortfall minimisation via an additive, increase-only weight update), with added robustness: it returns the best-seen weights, stops once the allocation freezes, and excludes zero-total features instead of aborting. It returns a structured elsar_calibration object (weights, representation profile, per-iteration trajectory, metadata) and writes no files. prioritizr and a solver (gurobi, or highs for a free/local option) are optional dependencies, checked at call time with an actionable message.

  • Sub-national region codes (e.g. "USA_CA") now work with global datasets: make_kbas(), make_wetlands_ramsar(), make_urban_greening_opportunities() and make_protected_areas(from_wdpca = TRUE) filter or fetch by the national part of the code ("USA") instead of matching nothing.

  • make_protected_areas() drops protected areas outside the planning-unit extent before dissolving them. Using a national WDPA dataset for a small study area is now much cheaper (California: 48,010 of 50,976 US sites skipped).

  • New elsar_check_setup() diagnoses your installation tier by tier (core / protected areas / Earth Engine) and reports what is present, what is missing, and the exact command to fix each gap. It makes no changes, needs no credentials, and never errors, so it is safe to run any time - and its output is what the bug-report template asks Earth Engine users to include.

  • New elsar_setup_gee() bootstraps the Earth Engine environment in one call: it finds conda (and can install miniconda for you if you allow it), creates a persistent conda environment (elsar_ee) with earthengine-api, and optionally walks you through Earth Engine and Google Drive authentication. Run it once, ahead of time, instead of letting the first download_* call build the environment mid-analysis.

Installation / Dependencies

  • The core package is now much lighter to install. wdpar, reticulate, googledrive, and rappdirs moved from Imports to Suggests, so installing elsar no longer forces a Chromium browser, libarchive, conda/Python, or two Google OAuth flows on users who only need the core (boundaries, planning units, normalisation, zone builders from local rasters, plotting). The optional features now check for their packages and give an actionable install message when one is missing:
    • make_protected_areas(from_wdpca = TRUE) requires wdpar;
    • the download_* (Earth Engine) functions require reticulate and googledrive (run elsar_setup_gee() to configure them).
  • scales and png moved from Suggests to Imports: they are used unconditionally by the core plotting functions, so they belong there.

Improvements

  • median_from_rast() errors now say how to fix a missing or histogram-less GDAL side-car: they give the gdalinfo -hist command (and the sf::gdal_utils() equivalent) for the exact file terra opened, with a rough time estimate for large rasters. Previously the message was only “Side-car XML not found for ”, which surfaced mid-run in make_threatened_ecosystems_protection() with no hint.

  • The Earth Engine conda environment is now persistent and reused across sessions rather than created per-process and removed after each download. Previously each download_* call could build a gee_temp_env_<pid> environment and delete it on exit, re-downloading Python and earthengine-api every session (and, if a run was interrupted before cleanup, leaving stray gee_temp_env_* environments behind). initialize_earthengine() now creates and reuses the stable elsar_ee environment.

  • Conda detection (find_conda_base()) now also consults reticulate (its managed miniconda, conda_binary(), miniconda_path()), so installations in non-standard locations - including a reticulate-installed miniconda and micromamba/Homebrew installs - are found instead of triggering “Could not find conda installation”.

elsar 0.4.0

Breaking Changes

  • Zone-function parameters were harmonised for a coherent API. The human-pressure input is now human_pressure everywhere (was hii_input in make_protect_zone(), make_manage_zone(), make_degraded_areas()); raw input rasters use bare names without the _input suffix (agricultural_areas, built_areas, pasturelands, managed_forests - previously *_input); make_degraded_areas() now takes iso3/pus (was country_iso/pu); the built-area threshold is built_areas_threshold everywhere (was built_area_threshold in make_restore_zone() / make_urban_greening_zone()); and make_restore_zone()’s patch filter is filter_patch_size (was filter_small_patches). Callers must update named arguments accordingly.

  • make_degraded_areas() writes its final output as degraded_areas_{iso3}.tif (was restore_zone_{iso3}.tif, which was easily confused with make_restore_zone()’s restore_zones_{iso3}.tif).

New Features

  • The zone builders (make_protect_zone(), make_restore_zone(), make_manage_zone(), make_urban_greening_zone()) now write their region-aligned intermediate input layers to output_path when it is supplied, alongside the final zone raster - matching what make_degraded_areas() already did. The files written are, per function:
    • protect: agriculture_areas_, built_areas_, human_pressure_
    • restore: agriculture_areas_, built_areas_, human_pressure_, degradation_, forest_mask_
    • manage: agriculture_areas_, pasturelands_, built_areas_, hii_mid60pct_, managed_forests_
    • urban greening: built_areas_ Each intermediate is terra::mask()-ed to the planning units, so cells outside the study area are NoData (consistent with the zone outputs).
    NOTE: this changes the on-disk output for existing callers that pass output_path - they now receive these additional GeoTIFF sidecars. Callers who want only the final zone should point output_path at a dedicated directory.

Bug Fixes

  • make_degraded_areas() now writes its resampled agriculture and built-area sidecars (esa_agriculture_resample_, built_areas_) as FLT4S. They are bilinear proportions (0-1) and were previously saved as INT1U, which truncated them to all-zero.

  • make_restore_zone() now always saves the agriculture_areas_ and built_areas_ intermediates when output_path is set, including when they are derived from LULC (previously only saved when passed as explicit rasters).

  • make_normalised_raster() no longer emits a warning() on every rescaled = FALSE call (demoted to an informational message), and its internal output_path writer uses a valid INT1S NoData sentinel (-128) instead of the out-of-range 255.

elsar 0.3.1

Bug Fixes

  • exact_rasterise() no longer exhausts the OS open-file limit or crawls on vector layers with very many features. Previously it built one coverage-fraction raster per feature and stacked them, which is O(nfeatures) in both open file handles and time - wall-to-wall class maps with tens of thousands of polygons failed with “cannot open N files”. A new max_exact_features argument (default 1000) switches large layers with a standard fun (mean/sum/max/min) to a single terra::rasterize() pass; the exact per-feature coverage path is retained for smaller layers. A large layer with a non-standard fun now warns before falling back.

elsar 0.3.0

Deprecations

  • make_custom_projection() is renamed to make_custom_mollweide_projection() (the projection has always been Mollweide). The old name still works as a deprecated alias that warns.

New Features

  • Regional / sub-national planning runs: iso3 may carry a suffix (e.g. "ECU_REG", "ECU-GEF8"). is_valid_iso3() and the functions that validate it now accept these custom regional codes, which rely on a supplied boundary rather than an ISO lookup.

  • make_boundary() and make_custom_mollweide_projection() support whole-file regional boundaries: use a custom boundary with no ISO3 column, dissolving multiple features into a single planning region.

  • save_raster() now builds overviews (OVERVIEWS=AUTO) so outputs are fully valid Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs, and gains an overview-resampling override (resampling=, e.g. "mode" for categorical layers).

  • make_protected_areas() tolerates custom local protected-area layers that lack the WDPCA schema (STATUS / SITE_TYPE / MAB filters apply only when those columns exist).

Bug Fixes

  • make_custom_mollweide_projection() computes the projection centre in WGS84, fixing a wrong central meridian when the input boundary is in a projected CRS (e.g. UTM); it also tolerates a NULL iso3.

  • CRS-aware spatial filter: elsar_load_data() / filter_sf() reproject the wkt_filter geometry into each layer’s own CRS before filtering, so a filter built in one CRS no longer returns zero features against a layer stored in another (e.g. a Mollweide gpkg vs planning units on a different central meridian).

  • make_normalised_raster() masks unflagged NoData sentinels (e.g. -2147483648, -2147483647) that would otherwise dominate the 0-1 rescale and flatten real values to ~1; it warns when it does.

elsar 0.2.0

Breaking Changes

  • Renamed from_wdpa parameter to from_wdpca in make_protected_areas() to reflect the rename of the World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) to the World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas (WDPCA).

New Features

  • Added file naming conventions vignette documenting standardised naming patterns for ELSA pipeline inputs, outputs, and figures.

  • Added dark mode toggle to the pkgdown website.

  • Added make_urban_greening_zone() to the pkgdown reference index.

  • make_protect_zone() now adapts the HII threshold when mean HII inside protected areas is high (>= 4). Uses the PA mean as the threshold instead of the quantile-based approach to avoid excluding nearly all areas in high-HFI countries (#79). hii_input is now optional.

Improvements

  • Updated Global Data Processing Reference vignette:
    • Fixed stale and incorrect function names.
    • Added missing datasets (degraded areas, flood abatement, indigenous managed lands).
    • Added “Since” column tracking which version introduced each function.
    • Documented removed/deprecated datasets in a dedicated section.
  • Added version tracking column to the dataset reference table.

Internal Changes

  • Bumped version to 0.1.0 to reflect API stability.

elsar 0.0.7

New Features

  • Added Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) download functions for multiple data products:

    • download_lulc_data() - unified interface for LULC data
    • download_dynamic_world_data() - Google Dynamic World
    • download_esa_worldcover_data() - ESA WorldCover
    • download_esri_lulc_data() - ESRI Land Cover
    • download_lulc_class_proportion() and download_lulc_proportions() - class proportion calculations

  • Added GEE/conda helper functions for improved Google Earth Engine integration:

    • create_gee_conda_env() - automated conda environment setup

    • find_conda_base() and find_env_python() - conda path utilities

    • get_crs_wkt() - CRS WKT string extraction

  • Added multi-LULC product support with GEE-side aggregation

  • Exported check_and_download_required_layers() for checking and downloading required data layers

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” error in make_urban_greening_opportunities() when input data contains NA values in filter columns

  • Fixed “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” error in make_normalised_raster() when checking for empty raster values

  • Fixed “[subset] no (valid) layer selected” error in get_binary_layers() when raster stack has zero layers or when subsetting returns empty indices

  • Fixed “Python int too large to convert to C long” error on Windows when accessing GEE task status (timestamps exceed 32-bit integer range)

  • Fixed GEE multi-tile export bug where only some tiles were downloaded for large areas (e.g., Chile pasturelands). Now waits for all tiles to appear before downloading

  • Fixed curve geometry handling in make_ramsar_sites() for improved gpkg support

  • Fixed KBA geometry handling issues

  • Fixed extent alignment bug in zone functions (make_protect_zone(), make_restore_zone(), make_manage_zone())

  • Fixed operator precedence bug in make_threatened_ecosystems_restoration()

  • Fixed syntax error in make_restore_zone()

Improvements

  • Updated make_protected_areas() for WDPCA schema changes

  • Standardized logging and input validation across all functions

  • Improved package documentation and README

  • Sanitized filenames for saved plots

  • Added logging for HII threshold values

  • Refactored restore zone creation to allow single version output

Deprecations

  • Deprecated elsar_plot_static_raster_c() and elsar_plot_static_raster_d() in favor of unified plotting API

  • Deprecated get_iucn_ecosystems() and get_iucn_forests() functions

  • Deprecated pa_def parameter in make_protected_areas() - use status_filter instead

Internal Changes

  • Removed unused make_elsa_problem.R

  • Consolidated utility files (utils-elsa_plotting.R, utils-elsa_posthoc.R, utils-pipeline.R)

  • Improved logging function and standardized messaging

  • Added lifecycle, future, purrr, rappdirs, and xml2 to Imports
